title: A coherent sheaf with zero-dimensional support is supported on a finite subscheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-morphism-conventions], let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and suppose that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ has dimension at most zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\mathcal N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then there exist a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], a closed immersion $i:\operatorname{Spec}(A)\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and a coherent module $\mathcal G$ on $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [pqf-def-coherent] such that the underlying set of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, $\mathcal F\cong i_*\mathcal G$, and $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal N\cong i_*(\mathcal G\otimes i^*\mathcal N)$. In particular, $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal N$ is coherent and has the same support as $\mathcal F$. For every $q\ge0$, the closed immersion gives canonical isomorphisms $H^q(X,\mathcal F)\cong H^q(\operatorname{Spec}(A),\mathcal G)$ and $H^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal N)\cong H^q(\operatorname{Spec}(A),\mathcal G\otimes i^*\mathcal N)$, where cohomology and global sections are those of [def-pc-euler-characteristic].

source.place: Tag 0AYT (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof of parts (3)--(5): the annihilator closed subscheme of a coherent module with zero-dimensional support is finite over the field, and cohomology is unchanged under its closed pushforward

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X locally Noetherian. Apply isCoherent_iff_isQuasicoherent_and_isFiniteType to F and schemeTheoreticSupport to its quasi-coherent finite-type structure. The resulting annihilator ideal I has a closed subscheme j:Z -> X with image exactly Supp(F), and its sections annihilate F. A closed embedding identifies topologicalKrullDim Z with the dimension of this image. No preliminary enumeration of support points is needed.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof of parts (3)--(5), and Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0)

proof.text: Apply closed_subscheme_finite_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_zero to j and the structure morphism of X. Set A = Gamma(Z,O_Z) with the algebra structure induced by j followed by X -> Spec(k). This is the actual ring of global sections and is finite-dimensional over k. The affine isomorphism Z = Spec(A) defines i = isoSpec.inv followed by j. Naturality of isoSpec identifies i followed by the structure map with Spec(algebraMap k A); surjectivity of isoSpec.inv preserves its image.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof of parts (3)--(5), and Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0)

proof.text: The kernel ideal of i is the kernel ideal of j because isoSpec.inv is an isomorphism. Thus it annihilates F. The closed-immersion annihilation theorem says that G := tensorPullback(i)(F) is quasi-coherent and finite type and that the adjunction unit F -> i_*G is invertible. Both schemes are locally Noetherian, so G is coherent. This is the concrete essential-surjectivity argument inside the coherent-equivalence route; the full category/formal-module equivalence is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof of parts (3)--(5), and Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0)

proof.text: Uniqueness of left adjoints compares tensorPullback(i) with ordinary pullback. Pullback preserves invertibility, and the invertible projection formula identifies F tensor N with i_*(G tensor L), where L = tensorPullback(i)(N). Finite-dimensionality makes Spec(A) finite over k, so finite_and_discreteTopology_of_isFinite makes it a finite discrete scheme. On its singleton open cover, L is trivial; pullback compatibility with tensor and the right unitor identify the restrictions of G tensor L with G. The existing disjoint-cover biproduct isomorphisms and biproduct.mapIso assemble G tensor L = G, including the empty cover. Pushforward gives F tensor N = F. Transport quasi-coherence and finite local generators across this isomorphism to obtain coherence. Apply the module stalk functor to the isomorphism to obtain equal nonzero-stalk supports.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof of parts (3)--(5), and Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0)

proof.text: For any quasi-coherent M on the affine source, prove the module-valued cohomology comparison for i_*M degree by degree. In degree zero, rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf identifies both sides with global sections; the direct-image global sections are the source global sections with scalars restricted along i.appTop. In positive degrees, affine vanishing kills H(M), and the affine-pushforward cohomology isomorphism kills H(i_*M). The natural comparison with source cohomology transfers these vanishings to RingedSpace.moduleCohomology. Both resulting modules are zero, hence have a unique isomorphism, which respects global-function scalars. Apply this to G and to G tensor L (quasi-coherent by its isomorphism with G), then compose with the two module pushforward isomorphisms.
